title: Their little language
hypothesis: A specific funny-word question makes it easy to leave a personal reply.

slides.sub: Or is it a person, a pet, or a favourite toy?

What it means. How it sounds. A tiny story.

caption:

title: The first proper giggle
hypothesis: A funny specific memory invites stories without requiring a long answer.
photoAlt: A caregiver plays with a tiny sock puppet beside a baby's kicking feet on a warm-toned play mat. Illustrative AI-generated photograph.

slides.sub: Their sense of humour starts somewhere.
No judgement. We’d want an encore too.
That’s a detail worth keeping in their journal.
Tell us the unexpected thing in the comments.

caption:
Sometimes the funniest thing in the world is a sneeze. Or a sock. Or the same silly noise for the seventeenth time.

What made your baby properly laugh for the first time? If you don’t remember the first, what makes them giggle now? Tell us below.

title: The bedtime ritual
hypothesis: A familiar everyday routine gives parents an easy point of recognition and a short reply.

caption:
The song you know by heart. The little sway. The finger they want to hold. Every family has its own bedtime details, even when the routine changes every week.
